relations.subject: William Jones
relations.evidence: He was sent to Harrow School in September 1753 and then went on to University College, Oxford. He graduated there in 1768 and became M.A. in 1773.

relations.subject: William Jones
relations.evidence: In 1770, Jones joined the Middle Temple and studied law for three years, a preliminary to his life-work in India.

relations.subject: William Jones
relations.object: Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William
relations.evidence: He was appointed puisne judge to the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William in Calcutta, Bengal, on 4 March 1783

relations.subject: William Jones
relations.evidence: and on 15 January 1784 he founded the Asiatic Society in Calcutta.

relations.subject: William Jones
relations.evidence: He studied the Vedas with Rāmalocana, a pandit teaching at the Hindu University of Nadiya, becoming a proficient Sanskritist.

relations.subject: William Jones
relations.evidence: Jones kept up a ten-year correspondence on the topic of jyotisa or Hindu astronomy with fellow orientalist Samuel Davis.

relations.subject: Henry Thomas Colebrooke
relations.role: translation of digest of Hindu Law
relations.evidence: Jones's final judicial project was suggesting and leading the compilation of a Sanskrit "digest of Hindu Law", with the original plan of translating the work himself. After his death, the translation was completed by Henry Thomas Colebrooke.

relations.subject: Hendrik Arent Hamaker
relations.evidence: On 28 September 1822, the Dutch orientalist Hendrik Arent Hamaker, who accepted a professorship at the University of Leiden, gave his inaugural lecture in Latin De vita et meritis Guilielmi Jonesii
